candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows an immunocompetent 40-year-old with markedly elevated CSF protein (3.64 g/L), low-normal glucose ratio, and a corpus callosum mass with rim enhancement. The reference diagnosis is cryptococcoma (fungal etiology). Glioblastoma is a primary glial neoplasm — an entirely different etiologic and pathologic entity. While both can present as corpus callosum masses with rim enhancement, they are not equivalent and the fungal/infectious etiology is incompatible with a primary CNS tumor designation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Glioblastoma is a primary brain tumor; cryptococcoma is a fungal granuloma — different etiology and diagnostic category despite overlapping imaging features (corpus callosum mass with rim enhancement)

case_quality_flags: CSF fungal cultures negative yet cryptococcoma is reference diagnosis — diagnosis likely based on imaging and clinical gestalt; India ink negative may reflect low organism burden in parenchymal form
Elevated CSF protein with acellular CSF is atypical and supports parenchymal/granulomatous process rather than meningitis
